tickets.title: A land-repair replacement worker does not re-claim a partially landed flake ticket
tickets.what: Milestone review j07ff6cea6f157c6c finding 2 (run q69ce631dff1b534b). `dispatchLandRepair` copies the original ticket into the replacement job (`src/mcp/dispatch/orchestrator.ts` ~155-158, ~909-925, ~1855-1881). When the source report leaves an acceptance item under Not done and the replacement fixes a failing gate, the completed partial land belongs to the source (`src/mcp/land-records.ts` ~75-97). `src/mcp/flake-admission.ts` ~65-77 releases the source's claim, but the settled replacement has no land receipt under its own ID, so it adds the same ticket back to `claimedTickets`; `hud_tickets ready` then omits it (`src/mcp/local-tickets.ts` ~489-491) until retention and a follow-up queue cannot pick it up. Treat a land-repair job as part of its owning land attempt, not an independent dispatch. Verify line numbers at HEAD first.

acceptance.text: Test: admission stays blocked while the land repair runs and reopens after the confirmed partial land, with both the source and repair job receipts retained
hud_tickets ready lists the partially landed flake ticket after the repair settles

tickets.title: Fold graph helpers onto the owning node
tickets.what: Review jbce97a18f5eb2838 #2: a graph land node reuses its input worker's job ID (`src/collectors/execution-runs.ts` ~1227); the fold in `src/collectors/execution.ts` ~473 picks the last node per ID, so `build`'s helpers show on waiting `publish`. Prefer the owning (non-land) node. Drop the tautological `.length === 4` assert in `tests/unit/execution-runs.test.mjs` ~954.

tickets.title: A live run member keeps its folded helpers in Run Detail
tickets.what: Review j3a3a4af9a6d30f96 #1. `src/collectors/execution.ts` folds a settled helper out of Recent when its parent is live (`reachable` accepts `liveSet`), but the `otherSteps` loop skips a parent with `settledAt === null`, so a live batch item's helper shows nowhere in its run. Build the `otherSteps` row for a live parent from its recorded state (running); keep the 24 h cutoff for settled parents only. While here, replace the `seenRepairJob` set with a comparison against `ticket.jobId` (`isLastForJob` already picks one repair per ID); keep the source-row exclusion. Add a unit test: a running batch imp with one settled sonic helper.

acceptance.text: A running batch member with a settled sonic helper: the helper has no Recent row and Run Detail shows a selectable `+1 sonic` row for the member whose Inspector lists the helper's ask
Settled-parent behaviour and the 24 h cutoff for settled parents are unchanged
Unit test covers the live batch member case

tickets.title: A repaired graph check does not take its build's helpers
tickets.what: Review j3a3a4af9a6d30f96 #2. When `dispatchLandRepair` repairs in place it returns the source worker ID (`src/mcp/dispatch/orchestrator.ts` ~1862-1866) and `tickCheck` keeps it on the check cursor (`src/mcp/composed-step.ts` ~328-365). `readFixedExecutionRun` (`src/collectors/execution-runs.ts` ~1229-1237) marks only land nodes as `borrowedJob`, so the check node wins the fold in `src/collectors/execution.ts` and the build's helpers move to it. Mark a check node whose job ID equals its input step's job ID as borrowing it; a check with a distinct replacement job still owns that job's helpers. Add unit tests for a check with an in-place repair cursor and one with a distinct replacement job.

acceptance.text: A graph check whose repair cursor reuses the build job ID shows no folded helpers; the build node keeps them
A check repaired by a distinct replacement job shows that job's helpers on the check node

tickets.title: An indexed flake refusal is delivered even when job.json exceeds 64 KiB
tickets.what: Review j3a3a4af9a6d30f96 #3. `flakeBlockEvents` (`src/workflows/events.ts` ~30-33) reads indexed receipts with `cache.readJob` and skips every non-`ok` result; the cache caps JSON at 65,536 bytes (`src/roles/job-index-cache.ts`), while the watcher supports larger receipts (`src/runtime/watch-runtime.ts` ~85-96). An indexed refusal on an oversized receipt never produces a notice. Handle the `truncated` result for indexed IDs only (for example a bounded full read of that one receipt, or store the recipient fields needed for delivery with the index entry), without scanning job directories. Keep the `.noticed` once-only claim, recipient and no-land-flow rules. Also prune index entries whose refusal is already noticed or whose job dir is gone, so a quiet tick stays O(pending) (lead jf3d19db9344daa4e).

acceptance.text: A valid refusal on a job.json larger than 64 KiB produces exactly one task-client notice, and none once a land flow exists
No job-directory enumeration is added to the notice tick; noticed or vanished entries are pruned from the index
Unit test mirrors the existing refusal test with an oversized receipt

tickets.title: A ticket write that would cross the 64 KiB feature cap archives done tickets instead of failing
tickets.what: Run q817cf4916491d787 lost its repair round because `hud_tickets add` on `chores` failed with "Ticket feature chores exceeds 64 KiB"; main then split by hand twice (chores-done on 2026-11-26/27, chores-done-2 in bdb22016). Long-lived features grow past the cap every ~30 tickets. Keep the cap. When an add, update, comment, landing record or repair add would push `<feature>` over it, HUD first moves that feature's done/wontfix tickets that no open ticket in any feature names in `blocked_by` (and never the highest-numbered ticket, because the next number is the last ticket's number + 1 in `src/mcp/ticket-store-ops.ts` ~147) into the archive sibling `<feature>-done` or, if that is full, the next `<feature>-done-N` with room (create it; same objective). Rewrite `blocked_by`/`repairs` refs to moved tickets in every feature, add the new sibling to the objective's Features line in `.hud/objectives.md`, and do it under the tickets lock in one write set that the sweep/commit path treats as HUD-written. If nothing can move, fail as today. `hud_tickets get`/ref resolution for `<feature>/NN` must still find a moved ticket (search the feature's archive siblings) so existing refs such as `chores/46` in reports keep working. Update docs/reference.md.

acceptance.text: Test: an add that would cross the cap succeeds, moves eligible done tickets to `<feature>-done` (or the next `-done-N` when full), keeps the highest-numbered ticket, and the next add gets the next number
Test: open tickets' blocked_by/repairs refs to moved tickets are rewritten, and `hud_tickets get` with `feature/NN` finds a moved ticket
Test: a land's ticket record that would cross the cap archives instead of failing the land
The objective's Features line lists the new sibling; docs/reference.md describes archiving
